stories.lesson: A public milestone can carry a special responsibility to the community it represents.

stories.text: Rishi Sunak described William Wilberforce campaigning as a backbench MP for about 20 years before Parliament passed a slave-trade bill, then about 20 more years before slavery was declared illegal.
stories.speaker: Rishi Sunak
stories.lesson: Long institutional campaigns can deliver major change without the top office.

stories.text: Akshata Murty said that, at 23, she wrote her Stanford application essay about Mumbai's monsoon and how unequal shelter shaped her interest in equality of opportunity.

stories.lesson: A concrete experience can clarify a lasting social aim.

stories.text: Irfan said his family put him in charge of selling their Infantry Cross Road property around 1980; reinvesting the proceeds and flipping plots led him into real estate.
stories.speaker: Irfan
stories.lesson: Handling a real transaction taught him the business before he became a developer.

stories.text: Irfan said his first Bangalore mall opened in February 2004, shortly after his father died, and drew daily crowds that reached tens of thousands because organized retail was new to visitors.
stories.speaker: Irfan
stories.lesson: A new retail format can create demand beyond initial forecasts.

stories.text: Karan said his coworking team initially spent more to copy spaces from abroad, then localized its supply chain and lowered its fit-out spending per square foot.
stories.speaker: Karan
stories.lesson: Localizing procurement can improve unit economics without giving up the product.

insights.text: Jobs reduce poverty by supplying income and giving people hope and a productive role in society.

insights.text: Entrepreneurs and private enterprises create most jobs; governments enable them through infrastructure, human capital, rules, and governance.

insights.text: Productive electricity access supports businesses such as barber shops and hatcheries more directly than a household light and fan alone.

insights.text: Primary healthcare can improve outcomes, avoid later disease costs, and create jobs across a range of medical skills.

insights.text: Processing local raw materials and agricultural products locally creates better jobs than exporting them for processing elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Ajay Banga

stories.lesson: Simple digital tools can turn agricultural information into a practical decision.

stories.text: Ajay Banga said he left candidacy for Citi's chief executive job to lead the much smaller Mastercard, a risk he cited while discussing how to act on luck.
stories.speaker: Ajay Banga
stories.lesson: A smaller organization can be the better career opportunity when its trajectory is stronger.

stories.text: Seema described getting a breast-cancer diagnosis, searching across hospitals for the right oncologist, undergoing surgery, and finding that her mental state received little attention.
stories.speaker: Seema
stories.lesson: Cancer navigation should include specialist choice and emotional support.

insights.text: A large domestic market can make international expansion less urgent even for a successful Indian company.
insights.speaker: Martin Escobari

insights.text: Digitalization, healthcare change, energy transition, and rising consumers in the global south are long-running sources of entrepreneurial opportunity.
insights.speaker: Martin Escobari

insights.text: Lower launch and distribution costs improve the odds that local consumer brands can beat imported brands.
insights.speaker: Martin Escobari

insights.text: For AI investment, demonstrate useful applications and viable unit economics before committing heavily at exuberant valuations.
insights.speaker: Martin Escobari

insights.text: An Indian company's first global success can create a role-model effect that makes other founders more willing to build internationally.
insights.speaker: Martin Escobari

stories.text: Martin Escobari said his father fled a Bolivian farm during the 1952 revolution after the house was burned and thousands of sheep were slaughtered; he then worked as a public-service doctor in rural Bolivia.
stories.speaker: Martin Escobari
stories.lesson: Family experience of upheaval shaped Martin's view of fragility and resilience.

stories.text: Martin Escobari said his Brazilian ecommerce company had filed for an IPO, but the market crashed three weeks before it; after layoffs and a failed $25 million sale, the company cut growth to reach profitability and later went public.
stories.speaker: Martin Escobari
stories.lesson: Financial discipline can keep a company alive when capital markets close.

stories.text: Arian said he emailed Sam Altman as a teenager with examples of projects he had built; Altman first replied that he was busy, and Arian's later follow-ups led to a meeting in San Francisco.
stories.speaker: Arian
stories.lesson: Specific work samples and persistence can make cold outreach effective.
